title: Check yourself: what composition buys concurrent code

questions.stem: `TariffTable extends HashMap<String, Integer>`. A billing job, compiled against it, copies the table with `clone()` every night. A developer changes `extends HashMap` to `extends ConcurrentHashMap`, recompiles `TariffTable` alone and deploys it. What happens at the next nightly run?

options.text: The job copies the table as before, since ConcurrentHashMap inherits a public clone() method from its AbstractMap superclass.
options.says: AbstractMap's clone() is protected, which is what the error names.

options.text: The job fails with an error when it reaches the copy, since clone() is not public on the new superclass.
options.says: HashMap makes clone() public; ConcurrentHashMap inherits AbstractMap's protected one, so the old class file fails with IllegalAccessError at the call.

options.text: The job copies the table as before, since the JVM resolves clone() against the superclass the job was compiled with.
options.says: The call is resolved at run time against the classes now present, and the superclass there is ConcurrentHashMap.

options.text: The job fails with an error when it loads TariffTable, since a class file records the superclass of every type it uses.
options.says: The failure comes at the call to clone(), not when the class loads; a caller's class file names the method it calls.

origin.section: Callers That Know Only the Wrapper Run Unchanged When Its HashMap Becomes a ConcurrentHashMap

questions.stem: `ShelfIndex` wraps a map from item code to shelf. The unit tests build it over a `HashMap`; production builds it over a `ConcurrentHashMap`. The receiving desk calls `place(code, null)` for an item that has arrived but has no shelf yet, and `place` passes both straight to `put`. The tests pass. What happens in production?

options.text: The call throws NullPointerException at the receiving desk's line, since place is the first method to read the null it was given.
options.says: place passes the null straight to put; nothing rejects it until the map does, so the trace starts inside ConcurrentHashMap.

options.text: The item is stored with no shelf, since ConcurrentHashMap, like HashMap, accepts null as the value of a key.
options.says: The Map javadoc lets implementations prohibit null keys and values; HashMap accepts them and ConcurrentHashMap doesn't.

options.text: The call throws NullPointerException from inside ConcurrentHashMap, since that map refuses null as a key or as a value.
options.says: ConcurrentHashMap rejects null keys and values; the trace starts in ConcurrentHashMap.putVal.

options.text: The item is left out of the index, since ConcurrentHashMap skips a put whose value is null and returns quietly.
options.says: ConcurrentHashMap throws on a null value; it doesn't treat it as anything.

origin.section: The Swap Is Free Only for What the Wrapper Promises: HashMap Accepted null, ConcurrentHashMap Throws

questions.stem: A `CachingQuotes` decorator wraps a quote service that is safe to share between threads. It adds `private long hits;` and runs `hits++` for every answer it serves from its own cache. Twelve threads call it during a load test, and after all of them have finished the hit count is below the number of cached answers they logged. Why?

options.text: The decorator's field is written by concurrent calls without a barrier, so each thread keeps its own copy and the final read sees one thread's hits.
options.says: The page's long counters ended at about three quarters of the calls, far more than one thread's share; the loss comes from increments that overwrote each other.

options.text: The wrapped service is safe to share, so the decorator is safe too, and the threads must have logged some cached answers twice.
options.says: The decorator is a new object with its own state; the page's long counters lost a quarter of the calls over a correct store.

options.text: The wrapped service is safe to share, so its lock also covers the decorator, and the count drops when cache entries are evicted.
options.says: The thread-safety of what a decorator wraps doesn't extend to the decorator's own fields; the page's long counters lost a quarter of the calls over a correct store.

options.text: The decorator's field is written by concurrent calls with no atomic step, so two calls can store the same new value and one hit is lost.
options.says: A decorator's own fields aren't covered by the thread-safety of what it wraps; ++ reads, adds and writes, and two threads that read the same value write the same result.

origin.section: One Metrics Decorator Serves Every Implementation, and Its Own Counters Must Be Thread-Safe

questions.stem: An order service builds `Map<Long, Order> open = new HashMap<>()`, passes `open` to a cleanup task, then hands `Collections.synchronizedMap(open)` to its request threads. Request threads add orders while the cleanup task removes closed ones. What does the wrapper guarantee?

options.text: Request threads are kept apart from each other but not from the cleanup task, since only calls through the wrapper take its lock.
options.says: The wrapper's lock excludes its own callers from each other; the cleanup task's calls on the HashMap take no lock.

options.text: Request threads are kept apart from each other and from the cleanup task, since the wrapper's lock is the HashMap object both of them call.
options.says: Only calls through the wrapper take its lock; the page's expiry job holding the HashMap ran beside the locked puts and size() came out wrong.

options.text: The cleanup task is kept apart from request threads only while one of them walks the map, since the wrapper locks walks, not single calls.
options.says: The wrapper runs each call under its lock; it is a walk, many calls, that the caller must lock.

options.text: The cleanup task is kept apart from request threads only after the wrap, since wrapping turns the HashMap itself into a synchronized map.
options.says: The backing map is unchanged by the wrap; the javadoc requires all access to go through the returned map.

origin.section: A Synchronizing Decorator Protects Only the Calls That Go Through It
